questions.cardText:
[Physiology and Anatomy] What is the strongest muscle in the human body? Strength is defined as pressure exerted per unit of muscle mass in this question.
A. The heart
B. The gluteus maximus
C. The masseter
Answer: C. The masseter muscle, or the jaw muscle, can exert a force of up to 200 pounds (90.7 kilograms) on the molars. This force is equivalent to the weight of an adult panda or lifting a standard motorcycle.
questions.de: Welcher Kiefermuskel gilt, gemessen an der Kraft pro Einheit Muskelmasse, oft als stärkster Muskel des menschlichen Körpers?
questions.en: Measured as force exerted per unit of muscle mass, which jaw muscle is often called the strongest muscle in the human body?

timeline.labelEn: The Guinness Book of Records lists a human bite of 4,337 newtons held for two seconds
timeline.labelDe: Das Guinness-Buch der Rekorde verzeichnet einen menschlichen Biss von 4337 Newton über zwei Sekunden

questions.notes: "Strongest muscle" has no single answer: by cross-section it is the quadriceps or gluteus maximus, and Wikipedia notes the uterine myometrium may be the strongest by weight in the female body. The masseter is the conventional answer for the jaw. The question names the jaw so the answer is unambiguous.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following animals has fingerprints that are nearly indistinguishable from humans?
A. Raccoon B. Koala C. Lemur
Answer: B. Koalas have fingerprints that are so similar to humans’ that they can be mistaken for each other in crime scene investigations.
questions.de: Welches australische Beuteltier hat Fingerabdrücke, die denen des Menschen so ähnlich sind, dass man sie selbst unter dem Mikroskop kaum unterscheiden kann?
questions.en: Which Australian marsupial has fingerprints so similar to humans' that even under a microscope they are hard to tell apart?

timeline.labelEn: Anatomists at the University of Adelaide discover that koala fingerprints are almost identical to human ones
timeline.labelDe: Anatomen der Universität Adelaide entdecken, dass Koala-Fingerabdrücke fast identisch mit menschlichen sind

questions.notes: The crime-scene confusion is hypothetical (no documented case); the evidence is the 1996–97 Henneberg et al. study.
